children: , the global investment bank and asset manager, reframed the rate outlook after its economists added another Federal Reserve increase in October, Reuters reported. The shares slipped approximately 0.1% to $937.26. The valuation picture is already demanding: the stock stands 13.04% above its $829.15 GF Value, suggesting investors are paying a meaningful premium to the GuruFocus estimate of fair value.

Goldman now expects the Fed to lift rates by another 25 basis points in October after policymakers raised the target range to 3.75%4%. Sixteen of 18 Fed officials see at least one more increase this year, while four anticipate two. That makes Goldman's new forecast important for markets, but it remains an economic call rather than any guarantee that policymakers will follow that path.

Another tightening step cuts both ways for Goldman. Higher volatility can drive more hedging, trading and risk-management activity through its markets franchise. But pricier financing can also cool acquisitions, delay equity offerings and pressure asset valuations. For investors, that tension now matters even more with Goldman trading above GF Value: stronger markets activity may help earnings, but the valuation leaves less room if tighter financial conditions weaken dealmaking and risk appetite.

title: Goldman Sachs Drops as Fed Rate-Hike Call Adds October Risk
